email.body1:
Jennifer, saw Nitro is rolling out the new AI Tools tab and Smart Tools across the PDF and eSign platform.

When the product surface grows like that, the RevOps bottleneck is usually signal-to-action latency: in-market accounts pile up faster than reps can work them, and leads go cold. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up on its own, turning signals into booked meetings: 3-5x more meetings per rep, every email auto-logged to your CRM.

I built a personalized signal play for Nitro off your tech-stack signals. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Jennifer, quick follow-up for Nitro.

Most outbound stalls not on targeting but on speed and consistency of follow-up, which is where measurable lift hides. Our built-in best practices alone tend to lift response rates 50 to 70 percent, with every send logged clean to the CRM.

Worth 15 minutes? I will walk you through a teardown of Nitro's current outbound and three changes I would make to cut signal-to-action latency and tighten reporting.
email.body3:
Jennifer, last bit of proof for Nitro.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and could not hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Nitro's reply rate likely compares to other software RevOps teams. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?
email.body4:
Jennifer, I will stop reaching out on this one, but did not want to leave you empty-handed.

If cutting signal-to-action latency without adding headcount is not a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Rolling out new AI features is its own kind of busy, and timing matters.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to your RevOps motion? I will tailor it to Nitro either way.
